# Communicating Technical Work

**Estimated time: 4 hours**

Technical work is only useful if you can communicate it clearly. In this activity, you will study two complementary aspects of technical communication: presenting ideas effectively and writing technical documents that are clear, focused, and valuable to the reader.

After completing this activity, you should be able to:

- apply basic principles of effective communication to technical presentations;
- apply basic principles of effective writing to technical documents;
- create practical checklists you can reuse when preparing future presentations and written work.

## How to Speak — 2 hours

Watch **How to Speak** and take notes.

As you watch, turn the main principles into a practical checklist that you can reuse whenever you prepare a presentation.

For example, at **31:47** the speaker discusses the “too-heavy crime”: slides with too little white space, too few visuals, and too much text.

Turn principles like this into concrete checklist items. Use the checklist both:

1. while designing your presentation, as a reminder of what to include or avoid;
2. after finishing it, as a final quality check.

## The Craft of Writing Effectively — 2 hours

Watch **The Craft of Writing Effectively** and take notes.

Again, turn the main principles into a practical checklist that you can reuse whenever you write a technical document.

For example, at **13:45** the speaker explains that writing should be clear, organised, and persuasive, but that none of this matters if the content is not valuable to the reader.

A useful checklist item could therefore be:

> Is this valuable to the reader?

Ask yourself this question while planning, while writing, and after finishing the document.
